name: Seychelles
summary: Five oblique bands of blue, yellow, red, white and green radiating from the lower hoist corner. Adopted in 1996, the rays suggest a dynamic country moving into the future.
origin: At independence in 1976 Seychelles used a flag with blue and red triangles divided by a white saltire. A one-party flag of red, white and green followed in 1977.
With the return of multi-party democracy, the current flag was adopted on 8 January 1996, combining the colours of the main political parties.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The sun, giving light and life.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The people and their determination to work for the future in unity and love.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: The land and the natural environment.

symbols.name: Oblique bands
symbols.description: Five bands fanning from the lower hoist corner.
symbols.meaning: A dynamic new country moving into the future.

history.label: One-party flag
history.note: Red and green with a wavy white band.

facts: It is the only national flag with rays fanning out from a corner.
Seychelles is the smallest African country by population.
The colours combine those of the Seychelles People's United Party and the Democratic Party.
